Lessons.Title: Dividing Polynomials
ExplanationParagraphs: Learning goals from authorized source: use long division and synthetic division to divide polynomials.
The polynomial division identity p=dq+r requires either zero remainder or a remainder of degree lower than the divisor.
Long division: divide leading terms, multiply the divisor, subtract, and bring down the next coefficient; keep each polynomial degree aligned.
Synthetic division requires a divisor x−k, uses the coefficient sequence including zeros for omitted powers, and outputs quotient coefficients followed by the remainder.
For ax+b divisors use long division directly or transform to x−k and adjust the quotient by the leading scale a.
Use polynomial quotient in geometric volume/area applications only where all divisor dimensions are nonzero and admissible.
Independent Edulytics cool-down: (a) Divide x³−3x²−4x+12 by x−3. (b) Divide 2x²+5x+2 by 2x+1. (c) Explain why zero remainder confirms a factor.
Independent Try It 1 — General long division. Divide 3x³−5x²+2x+10 by x+2.
Independent Try It 2 — Synthetic division with missing term. Divide 2x⁴−3x²+7 by x−1.
Independent Try It 3 — Find geometric missing side. A rectangle area A=(x+4)(3x−2) and width w=x+4; find its length.

WorkedExamples.Title: Polynomial long division by a monic binomial
WorkedExamples.Question: Divide 2x²+7x+3 by x+3, including remainder.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial long/synthetic division and check dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder.
WorkedExamples.Check: Reconstruct exact dividend from quotient, divisor and remainder.

WorkedExamples.Title: Polynomial long division by a general linear divisor
WorkedExamples.Question: Divide 6x³+7x²−16x+3 by 3x−1.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial long/synthetic division and check dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder.
WorkedExamples.Check: Reconstruct exact dividend from quotient, divisor and remainder.

WorkedExamples.Title: Set up synthetic division correctly
WorkedExamples.Question: Divide x³−4x²+x+6 by x−2 using coefficient row [1,−4,1,6].
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial long/synthetic division and check dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder.
Steps: Quotient x²−2x−3, remainder0; synthetic parameter k=2.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Quotient x²−2x−3, remainder0; synthetic parameter k=2.
WorkedExamples.Check: Reconstruct exact dividend from quotient, divisor and remainder.

WorkedExamples.Title: Synthetic division with negative k
WorkedExamples.Question: Divide x³+2x²−5x−6 by x+1.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial long/synthetic division and check dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder.
WorkedExamples.Check: Reconstruct exact dividend from quotient, divisor and remainder.

WorkedExamples.Title: Synthetic division with missing powers
WorkedExamples.Question: Divide x⁴+3x²−4 by x−1, including zero coefficients for x³ and x.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial long/synthetic division and check dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder.
WorkedExamples.Check: Reconstruct exact dividend from quotient, divisor and remainder.

WorkedExamples.Title: Use volume-to-height division
WorkedExamples.Question: A rectangular prism has volume V=(x+2)(x−1)(2x+3) cubic units; length (x+2), width (x−1). Find height.
WorkedExamples.Method: Use polynomial long/synthetic division and check dividend=divisor×quotient+remainder.
Steps: Height H(x)=2x+3 units with x>1 for positive dimensions.
WorkedExamples.Answer: Height H(x)=2x+3 units with x>1 for positive dimensions.
WorkedExamples.Check: Reconstruct exact dividend from quotient, divisor and remainder.

KeyConcepts.Title: Polynomial division identity
KeyConcepts.Definition: For nonzero divisor d(x), p(x)=d(x)q(x)+r(x), deg(r)<deg(d).

KeyConcepts.Title: Long division
KeyConcepts.Definition: Divide leading term, multiply, subtract, carry down, repeat.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Continue while remainder degree ≥ divisor degree.

KeyConcepts.Title: Synthetic division
KeyConcepts.Definition: Shortcut for divisor x−k with coefficient row including zero placeholders.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Use k with sign opposite binomial constant.

KeyConcepts.Title: Missing coefficients
KeyConcepts.Definition: A missing x^j term has coefficient zero in synthetic division.

KeyConcepts.Title: Remainder theorem preview
KeyConcepts.Definition: Division by x−k leaves constant remainder p(k).
KeyConcepts.Rule: Zero remainder means x−k divides p.

KeyConcepts.Title: Nonmonic divisor
KeyConcepts.Definition: For ax+b factor, synthetic divide by x−(−b/a) and scale quotient by 1/a.

KeyConcepts.Title: Polynomial factor test
KeyConcepts.Definition: A zero remainder certifies exact divisibility.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Nonzero remainder cannot be silently ignored.

KeyConcepts.Title: Complex synthetic root
KeyConcepts.Definition: Synthetic division with complex k can produce complex quotient coefficients.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Keep real and imaginary parts exact.

KeyConcepts.Title: Geometric applications
KeyConcepts.Definition: Unknown height or width comes from volume/area divided by known dimensions.
KeyConcepts.Rule: State physical restrictions such as nonzero positive lengths.

SummaryPoints: Division identity p=dq+r must be preserved.
Long division works for every nonzero polynomial divisor.
Synthetic division shortcut uses x−k and zero coefficient placeholders.
Geometric quotients require physically valid dimensions.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Use k=+2 for dividing by x+2.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Synthetic k is the root x=−2.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Omit zero coefficients in synthetic division.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Misaligns polynomial powers and corrupts quotient.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Include a zero for each missing degree.
State quotient and remainder and verify by multiplication.
